This report uses the canonical analysis-entry file
`Res_2_Data_for_Analysis/dat_focal_analysis.rda`. Baseline and EMA analyses are
reported separately. All analytic tables use list-wise deletion within their
prespecified variable set.

The corresponding Excel result is
`Res_3_Results/Table_S1_4_DescriptiveAnalysis.xlsx`. No CSV output is created.

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(candidate)) candidate <- dirname(candidate)
  repeat {
    if (all(dir.exists(file.path(candidate, c(
      "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability", "Step_2_Measurement_Models"
    ))))) return(candidate)
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) break
    candidate <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not identify the project root from the public Step folders")
}

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
frequency_table <- function(data, variables) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(variables, function(variable) {
    x <- data[[variable]]
    tab <- table(x, useNA = "ifany")
    data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      category = names(tab),
      n = as.integer(tab),
      percent = 100 * as.integer(tab) / length(x),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

complete_prompt_day_sum <- function(x, time) {
  if (length(x) == 3L && identical(sort(as.integer(time)), 1:3) && all(!is.na(x))) {
    sum(x)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
}

complete_prompt_day_mean <- function(x, time) {
  if (length(x) == 3L && identical(sort(as.integer(time)), 1:3) && all(!is.na(x))) {
    mean(x)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
}

available_mean <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

correlation_display <- function(r, p) {
  stars <- ifelse(p < .001, "***", ifelse(p < .01, "**", ifelse(p <= .05, "*", "")))
  out <- matrix(sprintf("%.3f%s", r, stars), nrow = nrow(r), dimnames = dimnames(r))
  diag(out) <- "1.000"
  out
}

random_intercept_icc <- function(data, variable) {
  model_data <- data.frame(Name_ID = data$Name_ID, value = data[[variable]])
  model <- lme4::lmer(
    value ~ 1 + (1 | Name_ID),
    data = model_data,
    REML = TRUE,
    na.action = stats::na.fail,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(check.conv.singular = "ignore")
  )
  variance_components <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model))
  between_variance <- variance_components$vcov[variance_components$grp == "Name_ID"][[1L]]
  within_variance <- variance_components$vcov[variance_components$grp == "Residual"][[1L]]
  c(
    between_variance = between_variance,
    within_variance = within_variance,
    icc = between_variance / (between_variance + within_variance)
  )
}

two_level_descriptives <- function(data, variables, labels) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(variables, function(variable) {
    x <- data[[variable]]
    person_mean <- ave(x, data$Name_ID, FUN = mean)
    unique_person_means <- tapply(x, data$Name_ID, mean)
    centered <- x - person_mean
    n_person <- length(unique(data$Name_ID))
    variance_components <- random_intercept_icc(data, variable)

    data.frame(
      variable = variable,
      label = unname(labels[[variable]]),
      prompts = length(x),
      participants = n_person,
      grand_mean = mean(x),
      overall_sd = stats::sd(x),
      between_sd_person_means = stats::sd(unique_person_means),
      within_sd_pooled = sqrt(sum(centered^2) / (length(centered) - n_person)),
      observed_minimum = min(x),
      observed_maximum = max(x),
      between_variance = unname(variance_components[["between_variance"]]),
      within_variance = unname(variance_components[["within_variance"]]),
      icc = unname(variance_components[["icc"]]),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}
```

# Baseline

Baseline variables are repeated across EMA prompts in the analysis-entry file.
They are first reduced to one verified-constant row per participant.

## Participant-level preparation and list-wise sample

```{r baseline-preparation}
baseline_demographic_vars <- c(
  "AgeInYears", "Gender", "Grade", "FamilyResidence",
  "ParentsMaritalStatus", "ParentsHighestEdu", "TotalFamilyIncome",
  "SiblingStructure"
)
baseline_item_vars <- c(
  paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18),
  paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7),
  paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7),
  paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10)
)
required_baseline_vars <- c("Name_ID", baseline_demographic_vars, baseline_item_vars)
missing_baseline_vars <- setdiff(required_baseline_vars, names(dat_focal_analysis))
if (length(missing_baseline_vars)) {
  stop("Missing baseline variables: ", paste(missing_baseline_vars, collapse = ", "))
}

baseline_constancy <- vapply(
  c(baseline_demographic_vars, baseline_item_vars),
  function(variable) {
    max(vapply(
      split(dat_focal_analysis[[variable]], dat_focal_analysis$Name_ID),
      function(x) length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])),
      integer(1)
    ))
  },
  integer(1)
)
if (any(baseline_constancy > 1L)) {
  stop("Baseline fields vary within person: ", paste(names(baseline_constancy)[baseline_constancy > 1L], collapse = ", "))
}

dat_baseline <- dat_focal_analysis |>
  dplyr::distinct(Name_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_baseline_vars)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID)

baseline_complete <- dat_baseline |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_all(dplyr::all_of(c(baseline_demographic_vars, baseline_item_vars)), ~ !is.na(.x)))

data.frame(
  original_participants = nrow(dat_baseline),
  listwise_complete_participants = nrow(baseline_complete),
  removed_participants = nrow(dat_baseline) - nrow(baseline_complete),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline preparation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Sample characteristics

Sparse categories are collapsed using substantively interpretable adjacent
groups. Original fields in `dat_focal_analysis.rda` are not modified.

```{r baseline-demographic-recoding}
baseline_complete <- baseline_complete |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gender_group = dplyr::recode(as.character(Gender), M = "Male", F = "Female"),
    Grade_group = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("^UG-", as.character(Grade)) ~ "Undergraduate",
      TRUE ~ "Graduate/Other"
    ),
    Residence_group = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(FamilyResidence) %in% c("Rual", "Township") ~ "Rural/Township",
      as.character(FamilyResidence) %in% c("CountySeat", "City") ~ "County seat/City",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ParentsMarital_group = dplyr::if_else(
      as.character(ParentsMaritalStatus) == "Married",
      "Married",
      "Not married/Other"
    ),
    ParentsEducation_group = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(ParentsHighestEdu) %in% c("NoFormal", "Primary School", "Middle School") ~ "Middle school or below",
      as.character(ParentsHighestEdu) %in% c("High School", "TertiaryShort") ~ "High school/Short tertiary",
      as.character(ParentsHighestEdu) %in% c("Bachelor", "Postgraduate") ~ "Bachelor or above",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    FamilyIncome_group = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(TotalFamilyIncome) %in% c("less than 10k", "10k-50k", "50k-100k") ~ "Below 100k",
      as.character(TotalFamilyIncome) %in% c("100k-150k", "150k-200k") ~ "100k to <200k",
      as.character(TotalFamilyIncome) %in% c("200k-250k", "250k-300k") ~ "200k to <300k",
      as.character(TotalFamilyIncome) %in% c("300k-350k", "350k-400k", "above 400k") ~ "300k or above",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Sibling_group = as.character(SiblingStructure)
  )

baseline_age_descriptives <- data.frame(
  variable = "AgeInYears",
  n = sum(!is.na(baseline_complete$AgeInYears)),
  mean = mean(baseline_complete$AgeInYears),
  sd = stats::sd(baseline_complete$AgeInYears),
  median = stats::median(baseline_complete$AgeInYears),
  minimum = min(baseline_complete$AgeInYears),
  maximum = max(baseline_complete$AgeInYears),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

baseline_demographic_frequencies <- frequency_table(
  baseline_complete,
  c(
    "Gender_group", "Grade_group", "Residence_group",
    "ParentsMarital_group", "ParentsEducation_group",
    "FamilyIncome_group", "Sibling_group"
  )
)

baseline_age_descriptives |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline demographic recoding",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

baseline_demographic_frequencies |>
  dplyr::mutate(percent = round(percent, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline demographic recoding (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Psychological scale scoring and person-level engagement aggregation

Four baseline totals are calculated after list-wise deletion:

- Trait PSMU: sum of `V_BSMAS_1`-`V_BSMAS_18` (18-90).
- Depression: sum of `K_CESD_1`-`K_CESD_7` (7-28).
- Anxiety: the clean RDA is coded 1-4 while the scale documentation specifies
  0-3, so each `L_DASS` item is shifted by `x - 1` before summing (0-21).
- Perceived stress: `M_PSS_4`, `M_PSS_5`, `M_PSS_7`, and `M_PSS_8` are
  reverse-scored as `6 - x` before summing (10-50).

Six person-level engagement variables are added without combining behavior
types. For each type, a day is valid only when all three scheduled prompts are
observed. Duration is summed across the three prompts within that day, whereas
frequency is averaged across the three prompts. Each participant's 30-day
summary is then the mean of the valid daily values. Incomplete days are left
missing rather than treated as zero.

```{r baseline-scale-scoring}
pss_items <- paste0("M_PSS_", 1:10)
pss_reverse_items <- paste0("M_PSS_", c(4, 5, 7, 8))

baseline_scored <- baseline_complete
baseline_scored[pss_reverse_items] <- lapply(
  baseline_scored[pss_reverse_items],
  function(x) 6 - x
)

baseline_scored <- baseline_scored |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Trait_PSMU_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("V_BSMAS_", 1:18)))),
    Depression_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("K_CESD_", 1:7)))),
    Anxiety_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("L_DASS_", 1:7)), ~ .x - 1)),
    Perceived_Stress_Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(pss_items))),
    Gender_Female = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(Gender) == "F" ~ 1,
      as.character(Gender) == "M" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

engagement_source_vars <- c(
  paste0("mu_time", 1:3),
  paste0("mu_frequency", 1:3)
)
missing_engagement_vars <- setdiff(
  c("Name_ID", "Day", "Time", engagement_source_vars),
  names(dat_focal_analysis)
)
if (length(missing_engagement_vars)) {
  stop("Missing engagement variables: ", paste(missing_engagement_vars, collapse = ", "))
}

engagement_scaffold_audit <- dat_focal_analysis |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID, Day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    prompts = dplyr::n(),
    distinct_times = dplyr::n_distinct(Time),
    valid_times = identical(sort(as.integer(Time)), 1:3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
if (any(
  engagement_scaffold_audit$prompts != 3L |
    engagement_scaffold_audit$distinct_times != 3L |
    !engagement_scaffold_audit$valid_times
)) {
  stop("The person-day scaffold is not exactly three scheduled prompts (Time 1, 2, 3).")
}

engagement_daily <- dat_focal_analysis |>
  dplyr::select(Name_ID, Day, Time, dplyr::all_of(engagement_source_vars)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID, Day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Daily_Messaging_Minutes = complete_prompt_day_sum(mu_time1, Time),
    Daily_Posting_Minutes = complete_prompt_day_sum(mu_time2, Time),
    Daily_Browsing_Minutes = complete_prompt_day_sum(mu_time3, Time),
    Daily_Messaging_Frequency = complete_prompt_day_mean(mu_frequency1, Time),
    Daily_Posting_Frequency = complete_prompt_day_mean(mu_frequency2, Time),
    Daily_Browsing_Frequency = complete_prompt_day_mean(mu_frequency3, Time),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID, Day)

daily_engagement_vars <- c(
  "Daily_Messaging_Minutes",
  "Daily_Posting_Minutes",
  "Daily_Browsing_Minutes",
  "Daily_Messaging_Frequency",
  "Daily_Posting_Frequency",
  "Daily_Browsing_Frequency"
)

person_engagement_vars <- c(
  "Average_Daily_Messaging_Minutes",
  "Average_Daily_Posting_Minutes",
  "Average_Daily_Browsing_Minutes",
  "Average_Daily_Messaging_Frequency",
  "Average_Daily_Posting_Frequency",
  "Average_Daily_Browsing_Frequency"
)

engagement_person <- engagement_daily |>
  dplyr::group_by(Name_ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Average_Daily_Messaging_Minutes = available_mean(Daily_Messaging_Minutes),
    Average_Daily_Posting_Minutes = available_mean(Daily_Posting_Minutes),
    Average_Daily_Browsing_Minutes = available_mean(Daily_Browsing_Minutes),
    Average_Daily_Messaging_Frequency = available_mean(Daily_Messaging_Frequency),
    Average_Daily_Posting_Frequency = available_mean(Daily_Posting_Frequency),
    Average_Daily_Browsing_Frequency = available_mean(Daily_Browsing_Frequency),
    Messaging_Minutes_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Messaging_Minutes)),
    Posting_Minutes_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Posting_Minutes)),
    Browsing_Minutes_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Browsing_Minutes)),
    Messaging_Frequency_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Messaging_Frequency)),
    Posting_Frequency_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Posting_Frequency)),
    Browsing_Frequency_Complete_Days = sum(!is.na(Daily_Browsing_Frequency)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID)

if (anyNA(engagement_person[person_engagement_vars])) {
  stop("At least one participant has no complete day for an engagement variable.")
}

baseline_scored <- baseline_scored |>
  dplyr::left_join(engagement_person, by = "Name_ID")

engagement_day_map <- data.frame(
  daily_variable = daily_engagement_vars,
  person_variable = person_engagement_vars,
  label = c(
    "Average daily messaging minutes",
    "Average daily posting minutes",
    "Average daily browsing minutes",
    "Average daily messaging frequency",
    "Average daily posting frequency",
    "Average daily browsing frequency"
  ),
  daily_operation = c(rep("Sum of three prompts", 3), rep("Mean of three prompts", 3)),
  complete_day_variable = c(
    "Messaging_Minutes_Complete_Days",
    "Posting_Minutes_Complete_Days",
    "Browsing_Minutes_Complete_Days",
    "Messaging_Frequency_Complete_Days",
    "Posting_Frequency_Complete_Days",
    "Browsing_Frequency_Complete_Days"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

engagement_complete_day_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(engagement_day_map)), function(i) {
  day_variable <- engagement_day_map$daily_variable[[i]]
  complete_day_variable <- engagement_day_map$complete_day_variable[[i]]
  complete_days <- engagement_person[[complete_day_variable]]
  data.frame(
    label = engagement_day_map$label[[i]],
    daily_operation = engagement_day_map$daily_operation[[i]],
    complete_person_days = sum(!is.na(engagement_daily[[day_variable]])),
    scheduled_person_days = nrow(engagement_daily),
    complete_person_day_percent = 100 * mean(!is.na(engagement_daily[[day_variable]])),
    participants = sum(complete_days > 0),
    mean_complete_days = mean(complete_days),
    sd_complete_days = stats::sd(complete_days),
    minimum_complete_days = min(complete_days),
    maximum_complete_days = max(complete_days),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

baseline_score_map <- data.frame(
  variable = c(
    "Trait_PSMU_Total", "Depression_Total", "Anxiety_Total", "Perceived_Stress_Total",
    engagement_day_map$person_variable
  ),
  label = c(
    "Trait PSMU", "Depression", "Anxiety", "Perceived stress",
    engagement_day_map$label
  ),
  theoretical_minimum = c(18, 7, 0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
  theoretical_maximum = c(90, 28, 21, 50, 900, 900, 900, 4, 4, 4),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

baseline_focal_descriptives <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(baseline_score_map)), function(i) {
  variable <- baseline_score_map$variable[[i]]
  x <- baseline_scored[[variable]]
  data.frame(
    variable = variable,
    label = baseline_score_map$label[[i]],
    n = length(x),
    theoretical_minimum = baseline_score_map$theoretical_minimum[[i]],
    theoretical_maximum = baseline_score_map$theoretical_maximum[[i]],
    mean = mean(x),
    sd = stats::sd(x),
    observed_minimum = min(x),
    observed_maximum = max(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

engagement_complete_day_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline scale scoring",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

baseline_focal_descriptives |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline scale scoring (2)",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Baseline correlations

Gender is coded `Female = 1`, `Male = 0`; its Pearson correlation is therefore
the point-biserial correlation. The correlation sample is list-wise complete
across all four psychological totals, the six person-level engagement averages,
age, and gender. Significance is displayed as no star
for `p > .05`, `*` for `.01 <= p <= .05`, `**` for `.001 <= p < .01`, and
`***` for `p < .001`.

```{r baseline-correlations}
baseline_correlation_vars <- c(
  "Trait_PSMU_Total", "Depression_Total", "Anxiety_Total",
  "Perceived_Stress_Total", engagement_day_map$person_variable,
  "AgeInYears", "Gender_Female"
)
baseline_correlation_labels <- c(
  "Trait PSMU", "Depression", "Anxiety",
  "Perceived stress", engagement_day_map$label,
  "Age", "Gender (female=1)"
)

baseline_correlation_data <- baseline_scored |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(baseline_correlation_vars)) |>
  stats::na.omit()
names(baseline_correlation_data) <- baseline_correlation_labels

baseline_correlation_test <- psych::corr.test(
  baseline_correlation_data,
  use = "complete",
  method = "pearson",
  adjust = "none",
  ci = FALSE
)
baseline_correlation_r <- baseline_correlation_test$r
baseline_correlation_p <- baseline_correlation_test$p
baseline_correlation_n <- nrow(baseline_correlation_data)

baseline_correlation_display <- correlation_display(
  baseline_correlation_r,
  baseline_correlation_p
)
baseline_correlation_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Baseline correlations",
    row.names = TRUE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

# EMA

## Prompt scoring and global list-wise deletion

The EMA analytic set requires complete data on all 18 source variables used in
the prompt-level scale means and six engagement indicators. Any prompt with a
missing value in this set is removed before all EMA descriptives, ICCs, and
correlations, ensuring a common analytic sample.

The six DASS items are averaged to form prompt-level Psychological Distress,
and the three two-item content domains are retained because the six-item single-
factor model showed weak fit in S1.3. Engagement time and frequency indicators
are retained as separate interactive, active, and passive measures.

```{r ema-scoring}
ema_required_source_vars <- c(
  paste0("PMU", 1:6),

## Two-level descriptives and ICC

`between_sd_person_means` is the SD of participant means.
`within_sd_pooled` is the pooled SD of person-mean-centered prompt deviations.
ICC is estimated from a random-intercept model as
between variance divided by total variance.

```{r ema-two-level-descriptives}
ema_two_level_descriptives <- two_level_descriptives(
  data = ema_complete,
  variables = ema_analysis_vars,
  labels = ema_variable_labels
)

ema_two_level_descriptives |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema two level descriptives",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )
```

## Multilevel correlations

Within-person and between-person correlations among the 10 nonredundant
variables are estimated simultaneously by `misty::multilevel.cor()`, which
fits a saturated two-level covariance model using `lavaan`. Psychological
Distress is the exact mean of all six DASS items and therefore an exact linear
combination of the three two-item domain means. Adding all four scores as
observed variables would make the model covariance matrix singular, so its
correlations are derived from the fitted domain covariance matrix using the
fixed weights `1/3, 1/3, 1/3`. Robust standard errors and two-sided z tests for
those derived correlations use the delta method and the fitted model's
Huber-White parameter covariance matrix. This preserves the original joint
10-variable estimates without treating prompt rows as independent.

The two levels are combined into one matrix: within-person correlations appear
below the diagonal, between-person correlations appear above the diagonal, and
every diagonal cell is fixed to `1.000`. Cells use no star for `p > .05`, `*`
for `.01 <= p <= .05`, `**` for `.001 <= p < .01`, and `***` for `p < .001`.

```{r ema-multilevel-correlations}
ema_nonredundant_vars <- c(
  "PSMU",
  "Perceived_Stress",
  "Anxiety_Symptoms",
  "Depressive_Symptoms",
  "Interactive_Minutes",
  "Active_Minutes",
  "Passive_Minutes",
  "Interactive_Frequency",
  "Active_Frequency",
  "Passive_Frequency"
)
stopifnot(setequal(
  ema_nonredundant_vars,
  setdiff(ema_analysis_vars, "Psychological_Distress")
))
ema_multilevel_correlation <- misty::multilevel.cor(
  ema_complete |>
    dplyr::select(Name_ID, dplyr::all_of(ema_nonredundant_vars)) |>
    as.data.frame(),
  cluster = "Name_ID",
  estimator = "MLR",
  missing = "listwise",
  sig = TRUE,
  p.adj = "none",
  output = FALSE
)

if (!isTRUE(lavaan::lavInspect(ema_multilevel_correlation$model.fit, "converged"))) {
  stop("The saturated two-level correlation model did not converge.")
}

composite_correlation_delta <- function(model_fit, level, components, targets) {
  parameter_table <- lavaan::parTable(model_fit)
  coefficients <- lavaan::coef(model_fit)
  coefficient_vcov <- lavaan::vcov(model_fit)
  weights <- rep(1 / length(components), length(components))

  free_index <- function(variable_1, variable_2) {
    hit <- which(
      parameter_table$level == level &
        parameter_table$op == "~~" &
        (
          (parameter_table$lhs == variable_1 & parameter_table$rhs == variable_2) |
            (parameter_table$lhs == variable_2 & parameter_table$rhs == variable_1)
        )
    )
    if (length(hit) != 1L || parameter_table$free[[hit]] <= 0L) {
      stop("Could not locate a unique free covariance for level ", level,
           ": ", variable_1, " ~~ ", variable_2)
    }
    parameter_table$free[[hit]]
  }

  add_gradient <- function(gradient, variable_1, variable_2, value) {
    index <- free_index(variable_1, variable_2)
    gradient[[index]] <- gradient[[index]] + value
    gradient
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(targets, function(target) {
    gradient_covariance <- numeric(length(coefficients))
    gradient_composite_variance <- numeric(length(coefficients))
    gradient_target_variance <- numeric(length(coefficients))

    for (i in seq_along(components)) {
      gradient_covariance <- add_gradient(
        gradient_covariance, components[[i]], target, weights[[i]]
      )
      gradient_composite_variance <- add_gradient(
        gradient_composite_variance, components[[i]], components[[i]], weights[[i]]^2
      )
    }
    if (length(components) > 1L) {
      for (i in seq_len(length(components) - 1L)) {
        for (j in seq.int(i + 1L, length(components))) {
          gradient_composite_variance <- add_gradient(
            gradient_composite_variance,
            components[[i]], components[[j]], 2 * weights[[i]] * weights[[j]]
          )
        }
      }
    }
    gradient_target_variance <- add_gradient(
      gradient_target_variance, target, target, 1
    )

    covariance_estimate <- sum(gradient_covariance * coefficients)
    composite_variance <- sum(gradient_composite_variance * coefficients)
    target_variance <- sum(gradient_target_variance * coefficients)
    correlation <- covariance_estimate / sqrt(composite_variance * target_variance)
    gradient_correlation <-
      gradient_covariance / sqrt(composite_variance * target_variance) -
      0.5 * correlation * (
        gradient_composite_variance / composite_variance +
          gradient_target_variance / target_variance
      )
    standard_error <- sqrt(drop(
      t(gradient_correlation) %*% coefficient_vcov %*% gradient_correlation
    ))
    z_value <- correlation / standard_error

    data.frame(
      target = target,
      correlation = correlation,
      standard_error = standard_error,
      z = z_value,
      p = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(z_value)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

distress_components <- c("Depressive_Symptoms", "Anxiety_Symptoms", "Perceived_Stress")
ema_within_distress_delta <- composite_correlation_delta(
  ema_multilevel_correlation$model.fit,
  level = 1L,
  components = distress_components,
  targets = ema_nonredundant_vars
)
ema_between_distress_delta <- composite_correlation_delta(
  ema_multilevel_correlation$model.fit,
  level = 2L,
  components = distress_components,
  targets = ema_nonredundant_vars
)

augment_with_distress <- function(base_r, base_p, delta_results) {
  output_order <- ema_analysis_vars
  augmented_r <- diag(1, nrow = length(output_order), ncol = length(output_order))
  augmented_p <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(output_order), ncol = length(output_order))
  dimnames(augmented_r) <- dimnames(augmented_p) <- list(output_order, output_order)
  augmented_r[ema_nonredundant_vars, ema_nonredundant_vars] <- base_r
  augmented_p[ema_nonredundant_vars, ema_nonredundant_vars] <- base_p
  augmented_r["Psychological_Distress", delta_results$target] <- delta_results$correlation
  augmented_r[delta_results$target, "Psychological_Distress"] <- delta_results$correlation
  augmented_p["Psychological_Distress", delta_results$target] <- delta_results$p
  augmented_p[delta_results$target, "Psychological_Distress"] <- delta_results$p
  diag(augmented_r) <- 1
  diag(augmented_p) <- NA_real_
  list(r = augmented_r, p = augmented_p)
}

ema_between_augmented <- augment_with_distress(
  ema_multilevel_correlation$result$betw.cor,
  ema_multilevel_correlation$result$betw.p,
  ema_between_distress_delta
)
ema_within_augmented <- augment_with_distress(
  ema_multilevel_correlation$result$with.cor,
  ema_multilevel_correlation$result$with.p,
  ema_within_distress_delta
)

ema_between_correlation <- ema_between_augmented$r
ema_within_correlation <- ema_within_augmented$r
ema_between_correlation_p <- ema_between_augmented$p
ema_within_correlation_p <- ema_within_augmented$p

dimnames(ema_between_correlation) <- list(
  unname(ema_variable_labels[ema_analysis_vars]),
  unname(ema_variable_labels[ema_analysis_vars])
)
dimnames(ema_within_correlation) <- dimnames(ema_between_correlation)
dimnames(ema_between_correlation_p) <- dimnames(ema_between_correlation)
dimnames(ema_within_correlation_p) <- dimnames(ema_between_correlation)

ema_combined_correlation <- ema_between_correlation
ema_combined_correlation[lower.tri(ema_combined_correlation)] <-
  ema_within_correlation[lower.tri(ema_within_correlation)]
diag(ema_combined_correlation) <- 1

ema_combined_correlation_p <- ema_between_correlation_p
ema_combined_correlation_p[lower.tri(ema_combined_correlation_p)] <-
  ema_within_correlation_p[lower.tri(ema_within_correlation_p)]
diag(ema_combined_correlation_p) <- 1

ema_combined_correlation_display <- correlation_display(
  ema_combined_correlation,
  ema_combined_correlation_p
)

stopifnot(
  identical(dim(ema_combined_correlation), c(11L, 11L)),
  identical(rownames(ema_combined_correlation), expected_ema_labels),
  identical(colnames(ema_combined_correlation), expected_ema_labels),
  all(diag(ema_combined_correlation) == 1),
  all(diag(ema_combined_correlation_display) == "1.000"),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    ema_combined_correlation[lower.tri(ema_combined_correlation)],
    ema_within_correlation[lower.tri(ema_within_correlation)],
    tolerance = 0
  )),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    ema_combined_correlation[upper.tri(ema_combined_correlation)],
    ema_between_correlation[upper.tri(ema_between_correlation)],
    tolerance = 0
  ))
)

data.frame(
  estimator = "MLR",
  significance_test = "Two-sided robust z test",
  nonredundant_joint_model_converged = lavaan::lavInspect(
    ema_multilevel_correlation$model.fit, "converged"
  ),
  psychological_distress_method = "Fixed-weight covariance derivation with robust delta-method SE",
  lower_triangle = "Within-person correlations",
  upper_triangle = "Between-person correlations",
  diagonal = "1.000",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Ema multilevel correlations",
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"'
  )

ema_combined_correlation_display |>

    escape = TRUE,

write_merged_heading <- function(wb, sheet, text, row, n_columns, style) {
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet, text, startRow = row, startCol = 1, colNames = FALSE)
  openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet, cols = 1:n_columns, rows = row)
  openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet, style, rows = row, cols = 1:n_columns, gridExpand = TRUE)
}

write_data_block <- function(wb, sheet, data, start_row) {
  openxlsx::writeData(
    wb, sheet, data, startRow = start_row, startCol = 1,
    colNames = TRUE, rowNames = FALSE, keepNA = FALSE
  )
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    wb, sheet, header_style, rows = start_row,
    cols = seq_len(ncol(data)), gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
  )
  if (nrow(data) > 0L) {
    openxlsx::addStyle(
      wb, sheet, body_style, rows = (start_row + 1):(start_row + nrow(data)),
      cols = seq_len(ncol(data)), gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
    )
  }
}

normalize_openxml_relationships <- function(path) {
  # Remove only worksheet drawing/VML relationships whose internal targets
  # are absent. Preserve valid drawings, external links and all other parts.
  unpack_dir <- tempfile("s1_4_xlsx_")
  dir.create(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  on.exit(unlink(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  members <- utils::unzip(path, list = TRUE)$Name
  unsafe_member <- function(member) {
    parts <- strsplit(gsub("\\\\", "/", member), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    grepl("^[/\\\\]|^[A-Za-z]:", member) || any(parts == "..")
  }
  stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(members),
            !any(vapply(members, unsafe_member, logical(1))))
  utils::unzip(path, exdir = unpack_dir)
  relationship_files <- list.files(
    file.path(unpack_dir, "xl", "worksheets", "_rels"),
    pattern = "[.]rels$", full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (!length(relationship_files)) return(invisible(path))

  resolve_member <- function(target) {
    target <- gsub("\\\\", "/", utils::URLdecode(target))
    if (!nzchar(target) || grepl("^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:", target)) {
      stop("Invalid internal drawing target")
    }
    parts <- strsplit(target, "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    result <- if (startsWith(target, "/")) character() else c("xl", "worksheets")
    for (part in parts) {
      if (!nzchar(part) || part == ".") next
      if (part == "..") {
        if (!length(result)) stop("Drawing target escapes the workbook package")
        result <- head(result, -1L)
      } else result <- c(result, part)
    }
    paste(result, collapse = "/")
  }
  drawing_types <- paste0(
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/",
    c("drawing", "vmlDrawing")
  )
  removed_relationships <- 0L
  for (relationship_file in relationship_files) {
    document <- xml2::read_xml(relationship_file, options = "NONET")
    relationships <- xml2::xml_find_all(
      document, "/*[local-name()='Relationships']/*[local-name()='Relationship']"
    )
    changed <- FALSE
    for (relationship in relationships) {
      type <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Type")
      external <- identical(xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "TargetMode"), "External")
      if (!type %in% drawing_types || external) next
      target <- xml2::xml_attr(relationship, "Target")
      if (is.na(target)) stop("Drawing relationship is missing its Target")
      if (!resolve_member(target) %in% members) {
        xml2::xml_remove(relationship)
        removed_relationships <- removed_relationships + 1L
        changed <- TRUE
      }
    }
    if (changed) xml2::write_xml(document, relationship_file)
  }
  if (removed_relationships == 0L) return(invisible(path))

  normalized_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  on.exit(unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  zip::zipr(
    normalized_file,
    files = list.files(unpack_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE),
    root = unpack_dir,
    include_directories = FALSE,
    mode = "mirror"
  )
  if (!file.copy(normalized_file, path, overwrite = TRUE)) {
    stop("Could not replace the workbook with its normalized OpenXML package.")
  }
  unlink(normalized_file, force = TRUE)
  invisible(path)
}

)

The 10 nonredundant variables are estimated jointly in a saturated two-level covariance model with MLR.
